subject: United Nations
overview: The **United Nations** was founded in **1945** to replace the failed League of Nations and prevent another global war. Drafted by delegates from 50 countries at the San Francisco Conference and entering into force on October 24, 1945, its Charter established an international legal framework grounded in sovereign equality and collective security. Built around six principal organs—including the General Assembly and the Security Council, where five permanent victors of World War II hold veto power—the UN grew from 51 original members to 193 member states, becoming the primary global forum for diplomacy, peacekeeping, and humanitarian coordination.

key_moments.title: The Atlantic Charter and Wartime Alliance
key_moments.text: Even before the United States entered World War II, **Franklin D. Roosevelt** and **Winston Churchill** signed the **Atlantic Charter** in August 1941, sketching a postwar system of general security. On January 1, 1942, 26 nations fighting the Axis powers endorsed those principles in the **Declaration by United Nations**, pledging their full resources to the war and promising not to make a separate peace.

key_moments.title: Dumbarton Oaks and Yalta Blueprint
key_moments.text: Following the 1943 Moscow Declaration calling for a general international organization, American, British, Soviet, and Chinese delegates drafted the initial charter proposals at **Dumbarton Oaks** in Washington. In February 1945, Roosevelt, Churchill, and **Joseph Stalin** resolved the remaining deadlock over **Security Council** veto procedures at the **Yalta Conference** and formally summoned the founding conference for April in San Francisco.

key_moments.title: Signing and Entry into Force
key_moments.text: Despite Roosevelt’s sudden death two weeks earlier, President **Harry S. Truman** kept the schedule intact, and 850 delegates from 50 nations convened in San Francisco from April 25 to June 26, 1945. After reviewing more than 5,000 documents, they unanimously adopted the **UN Charter** and the Statute of the **International Court of Justice**. Avoiding Woodrow Wilson’s League of Nations defeat, the U.S. Senate approved the Charter 89–2, and the UN officially came into existence on **October 24, 1945**.

key_moments.title: First Assembly and New York Headquarters
key_moments.text: The General Assembly and Security Council opened their first sessions in **London** in January 1946 with 51 nations represented, electing Norwegian Foreign Minister **Trygve Lie** as the first Secretary-General. After accepting a donated East River waterfront site in Manhattan’s Turtle Bay—formerly home to slaughterhouses and tenements—a multinational board of architects including **Le Corbusier** and **Oscar Niemeyer** designed the permanent New York headquarters, completed in 1952.

deep_facts.text: The name **“United Nations”** existed for more than three years before the organization itself. President **Franklin D. Roosevelt** coined the phrase in 1941 to describe the Allied powers fighting Germany, Italy, and Japan, and it entered official use on **January 1, 1942**, when 26 countries signed the wartime Declaration by United Nations. When invitations went out for the 1945 San Francisco Conference, only nations that had signed that wartime pledge and declared war on Germany and Japan by March 1945 were initially invited.

The UN had **51 original Member States**, even though only **50 countries** attended the San Francisco Conference. **Poland**—one of the original 1942 wartime signatories—had no generally recognized government in place during the spring of 1945, so delegates left a blank space on the Charter for its signature. Once a new Polish government was announced two days after the signing ceremony, Poland added its signature on **October 15, 1945**, nine days before the Charter entered into force.

Although the **Soviet Union** was a single sovereign state, it entered the UN with **three General Assembly votes**. Under a Yalta Conference compromise, Roosevelt agreed to grant separate founding memberships to two Soviet republics—the **Ukrainian Soviet Socialist Republic** and the **Byelorussian Soviet Socialist Republic**—and the San Francisco Conference formally invited both. In exchange, Roosevelt reserved the right to claim two additional General Assembly votes for the United States, a right Washington never exercised.

connections.name: World War II
connections.connection: The UN emerged directly from the wartime Allied coalition against the Axis powers, founded in 1945 to prevent another global conflict.

connections.name: League of Nations
connections.connection: Established in 1919 after World War I, the League served as the UN’s direct forerunner before collapsing after failing to prevent World War II.

connections.name: Franklin Delano Roosevelt
connections.connection: The U.S. president coined the name “United Nations,” co-authored the Atlantic Charter, and drove the diplomatic plans for the San Francisco Conference before his death in April 1945.

connections.name: Cold War
connections.connection: Rivalry between the United States and the Soviet Union frequently paralyzed the Security Council’s peacekeeping mandate from the late 1940s until 1991.

connections.name: Harry S. Truman
connections.connection: Assuming the presidency after Roosevelt’s sudden death, Truman refused to postpone the San Francisco Conference and oversaw U.S. ratification of the Charter.

findings.claim: The United Nations was founded in 1945 to replace the League of Nations and maintain international peace and security after World War II.
findings.explanation: Both the U.S. National Archives and the UN Charter page confirm that the UN was established in 1945 after World War II as the successor to the League of Nations to maintain international peace and security.

evidence.quote: The United Nations was established after World War II in an attempt to maintain international peace and security and to achieve cooperation among nations on economic, social, and humanitarian problems. Its forerunner was the League of Nations, an organization conceived under similar circumstances following World War I.

evidence.quote: The UN Charter codifies the major principles of international relations, from sovereign equality of States to the prohibition of the use of force in international relations.
